reason: The text names numerous characters who are not leaders. Michal (daughter of Saul) is named but holds no leadership position. Obed-Edom (the Gittite) is named and mentioned as the commoner who housed the ark. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, are named but are commoners—Uzzah dies when touching the ark and is explicitly not a leader. Abinadab himself is named but merely as the householder where the ark was kept. Additionally, David's multiple sons are individually named (Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet) as newborns in Jerusalem; while some (like Solomon) would become leaders later, at the point of their mention in the text they are not yet leaders. The named characters encompass common people, family members, and servants, not only leaders.
